newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks resume bull run and end on new record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks resume bull run and end on new record.

text.p: Swiss shares resumed their bull run, jumping nearly two percent to reach a new record close on the back of steady U.S interest rates and an easing Swiss franc.
"The U.S. Fed's overnight decision to leave interest rates unchanged was the first kick-off," one dealer said, noting that investors initially concentrated on financial companies.
A comment by the Swiss National Bank (SNB) that it added liquidity to the market then pushed down the Swiss franc and lifted the shares of industrial companies.
Another factor behind the strong rise was derivatives-linked buing, dealers added.
"Generally, we seem to have an upward trend," one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closed up 97.6 points, or 1.92 percent, at 5,178.6 with an intra-day high of 5,196.4 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 54.07 points, or 1.68 percent, to 3,268.35.
Most-traded UBS bearer shares soared 47 francs to 1,532 while shares in CS Group broke through technical resistance, rising 6.25 francs to 179.75.

Reinsurer Swiss Re stood out with a jump of 72 francs, or nearly four percent, to 1,906. The company said on Tuesday it expected net premiums to grow by 20 to 25 percent in 1997 and analysts were now finished digesting the impact.
Insurer Zurich Group underperformed the market, adding one franc to 485.50. Zurich Group said at the annual press conference it was confident that profits would show a doubl-digit rise in 1997.
Novartis was up 45 francs to 2,018, Nestle gained seven francs to end at 1,825 and Swissair gained 35 francs to 1,379.
